It grows feathers on your arms.

Only a layer of tree bark
Only the fingernails
Only the tongue

Why can breakfast help many kids at school?

It makes homework finish itself.
It replaces the need to drink water all day.
It turns books into toys.

Food provides energy for brain and body.
Regular meals support healthy habits.

They turn into water vapor.
They make the backpack lighter by magic.

Muscles and bones work together.

Water makes your shoes run for you.
Water stops your heart permanently.
Water removes the need for practice.
Sweating cools you but uses body water. Drinking fluids helps you stay safe and keep performing.

What does your pulse tell you?
How fast your heart is beating
How tall you will be next year
What color your eyes will become
How many teeth you will grow tomorrow
Each heartbeat pushes blood, making a pulse you can feel. Counting pulse beats shows heart rate.
Pulse is linked to heart activity.
Heart rate changes with rest and exercise.
What should you do before starting a classroom science experiment?
Read the steps, gather materials, and follow safety rules.
Guess wildly and skip all instructions.
Taste unknown chemicals first.
Throw away the measuring tools.

Safety comes first in any investigation.
What tool would you use to measure the length of a seedling?
A thermometer only
A musical instrument
A flashlight battery

Measurement needs the right tool.
Length is often recorded in centimeters or inches.
Why do scientists often record results in a table?
A table organizes data so patterns are easier to see.
A table makes plants grow without water.
A table replaces the need for any measurements.
A table erases mistakes automatically.

Organized data supports better conclusions.
Columns and rows make comparisons simple.

A rule that forbids measuring anything
A decoration on the classroom wall
A type of lunchbox

Repeating makes safety rules unnecessary.

A testable idea about what might happen and why
A final answer that can never be checked
A list of unrelated doodles
A broken measuring cup

Evidence matters more than guessing alone.

Controls make tests fairer.

Only what you hoped would happen
A random story with no measurements
Someone's favorite color

Evidence supports scientific claims.

Changing many things at once on purpose
Throwing away data you dislike
Skipping units on every number

Experiments never use any observations.
Observing always requires tasting chemicals.
Experiments forbid writing anything down.

Hide the mistake and invent a number.
Quit science forever.
Blame the plant for moving the ruler.

Scientists expect and check for errors.
Honesty is part of good science.

It removes the need for any control.
It guarantees the same result every time.

Keep other conditions the same.

Units are only for decoration.
Units make numbers unnecessary.
Units erase differences between trials.

So no one needs to measure anything
So safety rules can be ignored
So hypotheses become facts automatically

Grow plants without water or light
Delete incorrect safety rules
Replace the need for any observations

Labels and units make graphs clear.

Only other rabbits
